Q: What Python packages/libs are your favorite for automating prod level report building (graphs, charts) A:

While you'll likely be dealing with raw data rather than abstract functions, fellow Stack Overflow contributer @davide-sd has developed and maintains Sympy Plotting Backends (installable via pip install sympy_plot_backends) - the advantage of this package is that with one simple interface you gain access to Matplotlib, Plotly, bokeh and K3D-jupyter, without having to switch between different programming languages and with plenty of ready-made functions for every use-case.

It's very well documented here, and in case this be of use to you like it was for me, I built a PDF of the docs a few days ago, and have provided instructions on how to do so yourself in a PR.

It might end up being the best of both worlds for you, like it turned out to be for me!

Q: Is getting the general structure of code from AI cheating? A:

There are tons of linting tools or IDE's with formatters. To me that is basic tool use. If you are using a LLM instead of one of those basic tools, that might be ... kinda silly.

Anyhow, if you're trying to learn something on neetcode, but you just let a tool do it for you -- what's the point? On the other hand, if neetcode itself is just a tool, then maybe you can learn from what it accepts. It might be better to read some style guides for programming.

Q: Web scraping fails due to "request to load the app is timing out." A:

Bottom Line Up Front

"PhantomJS has not been maintained for the last 7 years, so it is likely it will not work with web sites that use more modern features." & PhantomJS has been suspended since 2018. -> Instead, I suggest using {chromote} or convenience wrappers like {selenider} (wraps chromote or selenium) or rvest::read_html_live which uses chromote. Better yet: POST/GET to their API because this circumvents all issues you have been having and is often faster. Studying margusl's answers on this topic will be enlightening!

On your question

  1. You are trying to access page 114 but the last page is 95: even if it would work, it would not make much sense.

  2. What you are seeing is the fallback page, when the real content can't be loaded by <script type="module" crossorigin src="/cdn/virtual-conference/assets/index-BqUYKt9W.js"></script>

I'd suggest using chromote / selenider headless browsers instead, which work properly. Then I still suspect this to be a xy-issue. That is why I provided alternatives below.

Old answer

The issue is the small initial delay at loading time. For obtaining the page's html, simply use rvest::read_html_live which uses chromote under the hood.

page <- rvest::read_html_live("https://virtual.oxfordabstracts.com/event/75765/people") 
Sys.sleep(2)
page |> 
  rvest::html_elements("html > *") |> 
  as.character() |> 
  paste(collapse = "\n") |>
  writeLines("page.html")

but I don't think that gives you what you want, which is likely participants and their conference-metadata. So I'd suggest doing

1) traversing the divs and creating a data.frame

library(rvest)
html_live <- read_html_live("https://virtual.oxfordabstracts.com/event/75765/people") 
Sys.sleep(1.5) # wait for initial page load

# extract cards data
get_cards_data <- function(html_live){
  # each author's cards
  cards <- html_live |> html_elements("div.shadow-md")

  lapply(cards, \(card){
    # for each card the author / symposium sections below
    childs = card |> html_elements("i.material-icons ~ div") 
    lapply(childs, \(x) data.frame(
      type = x |> html_elements(".text-xs") |> html_text(), # holds presenter / author
      event_name = x |>  html_elements("a") |> html_text(), # event names come from links
      event_link = x |>  html_elements("a") |> html_attr("href")
    )
    ) |> do.call(rbind, args = _) |>
      transform(
        card_title_name = card |> html_elements("h2") |> html_text(trim = TRUE),
        affiliation = card |> html_element("i.material-icons ~ div") |> html_text(trim = TRUE)
      )
  }
  ) |> do.call(rbind, args = _)
}


# list of resulting tables; 
# generally we should avoid growing objects, 
# but here it's just a relatively small list of data.frame references
tbls <- list()
# look for the next page link, that's the last child of the nav bar that has a valid href
next_page_selector <- "nav[aria-label='Pagination'] a:last-child[href*='page']"

cli::cli_progress_bar("Collecting card data")
repeat{
  tbls <- c(tbls, list(get_cards_data(html_live)))
  # stop if next page link can't be found
  if (length(html_element(html_live, next_page_selector)) == 0) break
  # click and wait for data to be loaded
  html_live$click(next_page_selector)
  html_live$session$Runtime$evaluate(
    "new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 600))", # you might need to set the timeout to something higher like 1000 ms, because this website loads in content via API calls and JS
    awaitPromise = TRUE
  )
  cli::cli_progress_update()
}
cli::cli_progress_update(force = TRUE)
# ⠇ Collecting card data 49 done (0.9/s) | 54.3s 
# bind tbls
final <- tbls |> do.call(rbind, args = _)

2) Using the GraphQL API

Behind the scenes the website performs post-requests to an API, fetching participant data as you navigate the pages. You can reproduce this using httr2. Here is how:

  1. Open the website
  2. Press F12
  3. Network -> Fetch/XHR
  4. Reload F5
  5. Look for graphql-requests
  6. check the Preview if that's your desired data
  7. copy payload
  8. Find your Authentication-Token here and content-type + origin for the req_headers() Note: request headers may vary from case to case, you can right click on graphql -> copy -> copy as fetch to easily copy the request
  9. Find Request-Url and Method

Now build a helpers to

  • make your requests req
  • bind a nested list that is returned rbindlist.v2

then perform queries and finally join. Please note: This is just a sample on the concept, your final approach might vary.

# httr2 approach
library(httr2)
auth_token <- "Bearer ..." # your Authentication-Token here. These expire!

# helper that queries "oxfordabstracts" graphql
req <- function(query, tok, operationName)
{
  request("https://graphql.oxfordabstracts.com/v1/graphql") |>
    req_method("POST") |>
    req_headers(
      "Content-Type" = "application/json",
      "Origin" = "https://virtual.oxfordabstracts.com",
      "Authorization" = tok) |>
    req_body_json(list(
      operationName = operationName,
      query = query,
      variables = setNames(list(), character(0)) # like {}
    )) |>
    req_perform() |> 
    resp_body_json()
}

# helper that flattens nested lists https://stackoverflow.com/a/68001784/28479453
library(foreach)
# this is really preference, you can also choose the purrr::map_dfr and pluck your nested list manually / rowbind / rbind-functions of your choice. Below code works very well for this case
rbindlist.v2 <- function(l)
{
  l <- l[lapply(l, class) == "list"]
  df <- foreach(element = l, .combine = dplyr::bind_rows, .errorhandling = 'remove') %do%
    {df = unlist(element); df = as.data.frame(t(df)); rm(element); return(df)}
  rm(l)
  return(df)
}

# maybe adjust the limit - in this case it's 2264
'query people_page_search {
  ordered_people_by_last_name_v2(
    offset: 0
    limit: 5000
    where: {_and: [{_or: [{presenting_at_least_one: {_eq: true}}, {author_ids: {_neq: []}}, {session_chair_ids: {_neq: []}}, {symposium_chair_ids: {_neq: []}}, {symposium_discussant_ids: {_neq: []}}, {poster_author_ids: {_neq: []}}, {speaker_ids: {_neq: []}}]}]}
  ) {
    author_ids
    session_chair_ids
    symposium_chair_ids
    symposium_discussant_ids
    poster_author_ids
    speaker_ids
    role
    first_name
    last_name
    name
    presenting_at_least_one
    __typename
  }
}' |> req(auth_token, "people_page_search") |>
  purrr::pluck("data", "ordered_people_by_last_name_v2") |>
  rbindlist.v2() -> p_search


author_ids <- p_search$author_ids |> unlist() |> unique() |> na.omit() |> paste0(collapse = ",") 

# here I query only for authors from author_ids in p_search
sprintf('query people_data {
  authors(
    where: {id: {_in: [%s]}}
  ) {
    id
    profile_picture
    presenting
    user(where: {name_badges: {}}) {
      id
      name_badges {
        avatar
        __typename
      }
      __typename
    }
    submission {
      id
      serial_number
      program_code
      event_id
      responses(where: {question: {is_title: {_eq: true}}}) {
        value
        __typename
      }
      symposium {
        program_sessions_symposia {
          start_time
          end_time
          program_session {
            name
            id
            start_time
            end_time
            event_id
            program_date {
              program_date
              __typename
            }
            __typename
          }
          __typename
        }
        __typename
      }
      program_sessions_submissions {
        program_session {
          name
          id
          start_time
          end_time
          event_id
          program_date {
            program_date
            __typename
          }
          __typename
        }
        end_time
        start_time
        __typename
      }
      __typename
    }
    affiliations: affiliations_without_hidden_responses {
      city
      country
      institution
      state
      affiliation_order
      __typename
    }
    __typename
  }

}', author_ids) |>
  req(auth_token, "people_data") |>
  purrr::pluck("data", "authors")  |>
  rbindlist.v2() -> p_data

# Join
final <- dplyr::left_join(p_search, p_data, by = c("author_ids" = "id"))

You will end up with a large table that needs selecting / cleaning / type-converting.

Q: Is there a standard naming convention for XML elements? A:

XML Naming Rules

XML elements must follow these naming rules:

  • Element names are case-sensitive
  • Element names must start with a letter or underscore
  • Element names cannot start with the letters xml(or XML, or Xml, etc)
  • Element names can contain letters, digits, hyphens, underscores, and periods
  • Element names cannot contain spaces

Any name can be used, no words are reserved (except xml).

Best Naming Practices

Create descriptive names, like this: <person>, <firstname>, <lastname>.

Create short and simple names, like this: <book_title> not like this: <the_title_of_the_book>.

Avoid "-". If you name something "first-name", some software may think you want to subtract "name" from "first".

Avoid ".". If you name something "first.name", some software may think that "name" is a property of the object "first".

Avoid ":". Colons are reserved for namespaces (more later).

Non-English letters like éòá are perfectly legal in XML, but watch out for problems if your software doesn't support them.

Naming Conventions

Some commonly used naming conventions for XML elements:

Style Example Description
Lower case <firstname> All letters lower case
Upper case <FIRSTNAME> All letters upper case
Snake case <first_name> Underscore separates words (commonly used in SQL databases)
Pascal case <FirstName> Uppercase first letter in each word (commonly used by C programmers)
Camel case <firstName> Uppercase first letter in each word except the first (commonly used in JavaScript)

Reference: http://www.w3schools.com/xml/xml_elements.asp

Q: How to resolve java.sql.SQLRecoverableException: IO Error: Connection timed out A:

We faced a similar issue, on Oracle 11g and Red Hat Linux boxes. The solution was to add these conf/run-time parameters.

-Djava.security.egd=file:/dev/./urandom
-Dsecurerandom.source=file:/dev/./urandom

The Oracle JDBC driver needs some random numbers to maintain a standard of security. For this it uses java to access /dev/random. /dev/random is run by the system and requires hardware interactions like mouse clicks and other keyboard interactions. You may add the parameter as is (note that /./urandom is not a typo).

Q: Error when running 'Install-Module': is not recognized as the name of a cmdlet, function, script file, or operable program A:

It sounds like you have a corrupted PATH environment variable. This can be confirmed by running this command:

$Env:PSModulePath -split ';' | Sort-Object

and looking for the below command's path in the list.

The following should resolve your problem:

Import-Module -Name 'C:\Program Files\WindowsPowerShell\Modules\PowerShellGet' -Verbose
Get-Command -Name 'Install-Module'

And a permanent fix:

[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable(
    'PSModulePath',
    [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('PSModulePath', 'Machine') +
        ';C:\Program Files\WindowsPowerShell\Modules',
    'Machine'
)
